title: Rudin Ch 10: Integration of Differential Forms

items.back: A map changing only one coordinate; a linear map swapping two coordinates. Every $\mathscr C'$ map with invertible derivative is locally a composition of these.
Continuous $ψ_{i}≥0$ with $Σψ_{i}=1$ on $K$, each supported in a set of a given cover.
A $k$-surface is a $\mathscr C'$ map $Φ:D⊂ℝ^{k}→ℝ^{n}$. A $k$-form is $ω=Σa_{I}(x)\,dx_{I}$, and $∫_{Φ}ω$ is defined by pulling back.
For $T:E→V$, $ω_{T}$ replaces each $y_{i}$ by $T_{i}(x)$ and $dy_{i}$ by $dT_{i}$.
Oriented simplexes, formal sums (chains), and the boundary operator $∂$.
$ω$ is closed if $dω=0$; exact if $ω=dλ$ for some $λ$.
For continuous $f$ on a $k$-cell, every order of iterated integration gives the same value.
For a one-to-one $\mathscr C'$ map $T$ with $J_{T}≠0$: $∫f(y)dy=∫f(T(x))|J_{T}(x)|dx$.
For a $k$-chain $Ψ$ of class $\mathscr C''$ and a $(k−1)$-form $ω$ of class $\mathscr C'$: $∫_{Ψ}dω=∫_{∂Ψ}ω$.
items.note: FTC, Green, the classical Stokes and divergence theorems are all special cases.

items.back: On a convex open set, every closed $k$-form ($k≥1$) is exact.
items.note: Convexity (or at least some topological condition) is needed.

items.back: Green's theorem in the plane, Stokes' formula for surfaces in $ℝ^{3}$, and the divergence theorem, all from 10.33.

items.modelProof: $df=ΣD_{j}f\,dx_{j}$, so $d(df)=Σ_{i,j}D_{ij}f\,dx_{i}∧dx_{j}$. Terms with $i=j$ vanish, and the $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$ terms cancel because $D_{ij}f=D_{ji}f$ for $\mathscr C''$ functions and $dx_{i}∧dx_{j}=−dx_{j}∧dx_{i}$.

By 10.25 and linearity it reduces to the standard simplex $Q^{k}$ with the identity map. There $ω$ is a sum of terms $f\,dx_{1}∧⋯\widehat{dx_{r}}⋯∧dx_{k}$; for each, both sides are computed directly with the one-variable FTC and compared.

items.prompt: Use Green's theorem to find the area of the ellipse $x^{2}/a^{2}+y^{2}/b^{2}≤1$.
Show $η=(x\,dy−y\,dx)/(x^{2}+y^{2})$ is closed and compute its integral over the unit circle.
items.hint: Compute $dη$ directly; pull back with $(\cos t,\sin t)$.
items.modelProof: $D_{x}\left(\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right)+D_{y}\left(\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right)=0$, so $dη=0$. On the circle $η$ pulls back to $dt$, so the integral is $2π$. Hence $η$ is not exact.

items.explanation: $η$ is not defined (let alone $\mathscr C'$) at the origin, which lies inside $D$. Stokes needs the form to be smooth on the whole chain. The integral is $2π$.

items.name: $η=\dfrac{x\,dy−y\,dx}{x^{2}+y^{2}}$ on $ℝ^{2}∖\{0\}$
items.details: Closed ($dη=0$) but not exact: its integral around the unit circle is $2π≠0$. The punctured plane is not convex, so the Poincaré lemma doesn't apply.
